children: Ahead of next month's WASDE, traders are keeping a close eye on what demand indicators show for U.S. grain exports. "Our focus remains on demand rather than supply," says Rich Nelson of Allendale Inc. For corn and soybeans, export sales are a key metric, while for wheat "psychological pressure" from the Russia-Ukraine talks is seen as having more of an impact, Nelson says, even with little progress in those talks. Most-active CBOT corn is down 0.7%, while soybeans rise 0.4% and wheat is up 0.2%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
